title: Applications of Nonlinear Projections to Rectifiable 1-sets
summary: Projection theorems in Euclidean space provide a fundamental link between the geometric structure of a set and the size of its lower-dimensional images. For 1-rectifiable sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$, a classical theorem of Federer shows that the 1-dimensional Hausdorff measure of such sets is controlled by the multiplicity-weighted lengths of finitely many linearly independent projections. We develop a framework for extending Federer's result into a diverse set of nonlinear problems.
